title: A clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a subcutaneous allergoid preparation of house dust mite allergens (Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus / Dermatophagoides farinae) in patients with moderate to severe allergic rhinitis/rhinoconjunctivitis with or without controlled allergic asthma.
official: A multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a subcutaneous allergoid preparation of house dust mite allergens (Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus / Dermatophagoides farinae) in patients with moderate to severe allergic rhinitis/rhinoconjunctivitis with or without controlled allergic asthma.
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the clinical efficacy of the active IMP for SCIT compared to placebo in adolescents and adults with HDM–induced allergic rhinitis, with or without concomitant asthma, after approximately 12 months of treatment, as assessed by the Adapted Rhinitis Combined Symptom and Medication Score (arCSMS)

interventions.name: Mometasone Furoate 50 micrograms/actuation Nasal Spray, Suspension

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Written informed consent has been obtained from the patient and, where applicable, from the parent(s)/legal guardian(s) in accordance with local requirements prior to any trial-related procedures (i.e. procedures not part of routine patient management).
2. Patients or parents/legal guardians willing and able to complete an electronic patient record during the Baseline Evaluation Phase and the Efficacy Evaluation Phase at the end of the treatment
3. Age 12 to 65 years at the time of informed consent
4. Medical history of HDM-induced IgE-mediated allergic rhinitis or rhinoconjunctivitis (with or without allergic asthma)
5. Positive skin prick test (SPT) result to either D. pteronyssinus or D. farinae allergens: - D. pteronyssinus and/or D. farinae test reaction (wheal diameter) ≥ 3 mm and  - Positive histamine-control reaction (wheal diameter) ≥ 3 mm and  - Negative NaCl-control reaction (wheal diameter) < 2 mm
6. Immunoassay result for specific IgE ≥ 0.70 kU/L to D. pteronyssinus and/or D. farinae
7. Clinical history of persistent, moderate to severe allergic rhinitis according to ARIA, defined by: Symptoms for ≥4 consecutive weeks and ≥4 days per week Symptoms considered troublesome and/or impacting daily activities or sleep
8. Clinically relevant symptoms of rhinitis or rhinoconjunctivitis) requiring regular intake of anti-symptomatic medication for at least 1 year before dosing
9. Scoring ≥5 when completing the house dust mite questionnaire (HDMQ).
10. Baseline symptom severity and medication use (eligibility for randomization): During a 14‑day Baseline Evaluation Phase, patients must fulfil all the three following:  ≥11 days daily documentation completed, ≥8 days, a total rhinitis symptom score of ≥6, or ≥5 with at least one severe symptom, ≥8 days documented use of rescue medication
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patients and/or, where applicable, their parent(s) or legal guardian(s), who are unable to understand the nature of the trial, provide valid informed consent/assent, or comply with trial requirements, as judged by the Investigator
2. A history of rhinitis, rhinoconjunctivitis or asthma to allergens other than HDM, likely to result in allergic symptoms during the time periods of the Baseline Diary and/or Evaluation Diary, when the following are present: documented sensitization (positive skin prick test [mean wheal diameter ≥ 3 mm] and/or specific serum IgE level ≥ 0.70 kU/L) and history of clinically relevant symptoms to allergen(s) other than HDM anticipated exposure to such allergen(s) during the time periods of the baseline and/or evaluation diary. For example, the following patients are to be excluded:  patients with clinically relevant symptoms to pets kept in the home, patients with clinically relevant symptoms to perennial allergens, such as moulds, cockroach, storage mites, patients with clinically relevant symptoms to pollen allergens such as parietaria, ragweed, cypress or mugwort, if these allergens are endemic in the region during the time periods of the Baseline Diary
3. Higher level of specific IgE to storage mites than the level of the specific IgE to at least one of the HDMs (D. pteronyssinus or D. farinae)
4. Clinically relevant chronic rhinoconjunctival or respiratory symptoms related to other reasons than allergies
5. Presence of any clinically relevant nasal disorder that, in the opinion of the investigator, may interfere with efficacy or safety assessments (e.g., hypertrophy of the pharyngeal/palatine tonsils, nasal polyps, or a history of paranasal sinus or nasal turbinate surgery). If in doubt, nasal endoscopy should be performed
6. Irreversible changes in the reaction organ (emphysema, bronchiectasis, etc.)
7. Forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) < 70 % of predicted normal values according to Quanjer et al 2012, under adequate asthma treatment according to GINA 2025
8. Uncontrolled or partly controlled asthma according to GINA recommendation
9. Patients with severe asthma corresponding to GINA Step 4 or Step 5, defined as requiring medium- or high-dose ICS-based combination therapy or add-on biologic treatment
10. Asthma exacerbation within the last 6 months prior to randomization defined as unscheduled doctors visit, hospitalization, or emergency unit visit requiring the use of systemic corticosteroids or change of controller medication
11. Severe acute or chronic diseases (e.g. chronic urticaria, mastocytosis, active tuberculosis, diabetes mellitus type I, malignant neoplasia, chronic renal failure), severe inflammatory diseases (liver, kidneys), acute viral and bacterial infections presenting with fever
12. Simultaneous participation in another clinical trial or participation in a clinical trial within 30 days prior to ICF signing
13. Autoimmune diseases, immune defects including immunosuppression, immune-complex-induced immunopathies (e.g. HIV, post-transplant patients, lupus erythematodes [SLE], vitiligo, Grave’s disease, multiple sclerosis)
14. Severe psychiatric or psychological disorders which, in the opinion of the investigator, may interfere with the patient’s ability to provide informed consent, comply with trial procedures, or adequately cooperate during study participation
15. Recurrent seizures (e.g., febrile convulsion, untreated epilepsy)
16. Laboratory values greater than grade 1 according to the FDA Guidance for Industry (Toxicity Grading Scale for Healthy Adult and Adolescent Volunteers Enrolled in Preventive Vaccine Clinical Trials). Normal reference ranges of the central laboratory apply. For laboratory values with age specific reference ranges of the central laboratory and when these normal reference ranges partly overlap with the toxicity grading scale (e.g. haemoglobin in young adolescents), medical judgement should be applied for in- and exclusion of the individual paediatric patient, and moreover values regarding eosinophils will be accepted also above the normal ranges because these values are considered as allergy marker
17. Current use of β-blockers (locally or systemically) and/or ACE inhibitors
18. Contraindication for use of epinephrine (e.g., acute, or chronic symptomatic coronary heart disease, severe hypertension)
19. Treatment with biologic therapy known to interfere with immune tolerance induction, including biologics targeting IgE or type‑2 inflammation, within the last 6 months prior to first dosing and during the trial
20. Treatment with antidepressants or antipsychotic medication with antihistaminic effects in the 6 months prior to and during the trial
21. Hypersensitivity to excipients of the investigational medical product
22. Previous randomization in this trial
23. Patients and/or their parents/legal guardian(s) who are employees of the sponsor, the CRO, or the trial site, who are involved in the planning or conduct of the trial, or who have any relationship of dependence with the sponsor or the investigator that may compromise voluntary participation
24. Institutionalized due to an official or judicial order
25. Female patients who are:  pregnant (confirmed by a positive pregnancy test), breastfeeding, planning to become pregnant during the trial, or who are of childbearing potential and sexually active but not using a highly effective method of contraception (defined as a failure rate of <1% per year), as judged by the investigator.
26. History of a confirmed anaphylaxis after an AIT injection
27. Current treatment with any kind of AIT or within the last 12 months before screening
28. AIT for house dust mite allergy within the last 5 years
